# Referral and networking outreach: the highest-leverage channel

Referred candidates get interviews at several times the cold-application rate. The play: for each company you're applying to, find one warm-ish person, send a short specific message, and ask lightly. Claude drafts, you send. **3–5 messages a week is plenty.**

## Where to find people (LinkedIn, about 5 minutes per company)
1. **Alumni from your university at the company.** This is the strongest angle. Go to your university's LinkedIn page, open the **Alumni** tab and filter by company. Or use People search with School = your university and Current company = the target.
2. **2nd-degree connections:** People search, filtered by company and "2nd". If the mutual connection is close, ask them for an intro instead.
3. **Early-careers / graduate recruiters:** search "early careers" OR "graduate recruitment" plus the company. Hearing from grads is literally their job.
4. **Recruiters who view your profile or invite you:** accept and reply the same day with template C.

## Templates
Keep connection-request notes under 300 characters. **Never open with "can you refer me".** Ask about their experience first; the referral offer often follows on its own.

### A. Alumni connection request (<300 chars)
> Hi [name], fellow [university] grad here ([course], [year]). I've applied for the [role] at [company] and would love to hear what your experience there has been like. Would you be open to a quick chat?

### B. After they accept
> Thanks for connecting, [name]! As mentioned, I've applied for the [role] at [company]. [One true line about your most relevant experience.] If you have 10 minutes I'd love to hear how you've found [company], and anything you wish you'd known when applying. No pressure at all.

If the chat goes well and it feels right:
> Would you be comfortable putting my name forward internally? Totally understand if not; the chat has already been a big help.

### C. Early-careers / graduate recruiter
> Hi [name], I'm a [university] [course] graduate ([grade], [year]) with [one-line experience], and I've just applied for [role/programme]. I wanted to introduce myself directly. I'm [city]-based and available [immediately]. Delighted to talk any time.

### D. Asking a mutual for an intro
> Hey [mutual], hope you're keeping well! Quick one: I see you're connected to [name] at [company]. I've applied for their [role] and I'm trying to learn more about the team before interviews. Would you be comfortable introducing us? Happy to send a blurb you can forward.

### E. Forwardable blurb (for D)
> [Name]: [course] grad, [university] ([grade], [year]). [One-line experience.] [One-line project.] Applying for [role]; would love 10 minutes with someone on the team. [email]

## Weekly rhythm
- 3–5 new messages a week. Log them below or tell Claude.
- Follow up **once** after about a week of silence, then let it go.
- Every accepted recruiter invitation gets template C the same day.
